Going into the week we are once again a little overexposed to the AI trade with fireworks at frontier LLM lab Anthropic and a somewhat dicey macro.

Wouldn't be surprised to see futures open down here when it seemed like we were out of the woods after SpaceXs giant IPO (implying solid IPO performance from Ant/OAI and probably follow through Capex) and a deal getting done in the middle east - the jury now appears to be out on both. That said, I expect both these concerns to blow over, especially Ant's issues which seem to be driven by shareholder Amazon, so expect this to be strictly transitory/deepseekish if we get a large drawdown.

Adjusted net exposure (counting leveraged ETFs with a multiple) is 92% long and I think I am still a little biased to short beta (Short $ARM alone has ballooned to -192k when adjusted for the ARMG multiplier) so it could be worse.

Overweighting to the AI trade is largely a result from letting our winners run - $INTC, $SNDK, and $HY9H (Sk Hynix). Although this is getting a little dicey, execution at all 3 companies seems to be solid and I think we have adequate earnings runway to let these ride until at least early 2027. I am running a short $KORU trade to short out a little bit of the $HY9H risk but otherwise letting the trade ride.

Solid wins in $PSNL and $DAVE have continued to provide us with at least some diversification in the larger positions in the portfolio and I have started building smaller positions in sectors I think are oversold - small cap Japan (not AI) and the US platform and SaaS ecosystems all seem oversold to me. And I will look to add to biotech in moments I think it represents good value.

I continue to believe $VEON is the most undervalued position in my portfolio. Ukraine is doing extremely well in the war against Russia, and if we get lower oil prices going forward I think it is just going to be over and $KYIV will continue its rise as an increasingly important company in Ukraine (already the most important internet company).

Most recently, $KYIV's acquisition of Uklon (the Uber of Ukraine) appears to be playing out very well, with an autonomous vehicle plan that has now been set in motion, and the recent launch of their marketplace platform (initial offerings include delivery flowers). It's not hard to see how $KYIV could become the most important company in Ukraine over time (if they are not already) - and I also see Ukraine's importance growing, with their expertise at drone warfare, potential EU inclusion, abundant natural resources (inc significant Uranium resource) and agricultural production, etc. Sustained lower oil prices dramatically reduces the Russia threat, and CL futures imply somewhat lower from here. Chevron sounds like they would be perfectly happy with $60 oil long term, but this would be a big swing in the relative economic strength of Russia. As the war ends, the dream would be a 50s America scenario, with sustained population growth and economic abundance. After non stop war, working hard for the Ukranian Dream would feel like a holiday.

Perhaps the fastest lesson I have learned lately is putting on a spread trade between the richly valued Tokyo Electron and the smaller Korean semi cap names. I think to make this trade the valuation discrepency needs to be very large and the right mental model might just be that people will always pay a large premium for the most important semiconductor name in each country (eg using $ASML or $AIXA to put on a spread trade when they are the only investable names in Europe is less likely to work). But it has been tough to find things to short against AI longs - just look at how people are using the very reasonably valued $NVDA as a funding short.

Anyway, we shall see what the week brings. Coming up later in the week I will release my next substack which focuses on the cancer diagnostics companies and the way biopharma is using frontier models.

As always, none of this is financial advice for your own portfolio, and feel free to ask any questions you have in the thread.

- $META and $MSFT strategies both a total train wreck despite spending literally infinite money. Google executing but still nowhere in coding, biggest win has been with TPU and their well executed roll out of Gemini into Search, not winning the frontier.

Neither of these are special "trading books" etc, generally I just put all my money in stocks because businesses are good at making moneys. A bunch of Korean AI infra plays not named Samsung or SK Hynix trade at major discounts to peers trading elsewhere. Here are a few that look interesting to me (as always, please do your own research):

DI Corp. (003160, $423M MC) and Techwing (089030, $1.22B MC) - Memory test semicaps with good burn-in and HBM exposure. Samsung and Hynix are major clients for each, with $MU also a major client for Techwing. Both firms trade for around 13x 2027E EPS.

ISU Petasys (007660, $5.2B MC) - A PCB maker with strong data center exposure across AI accelerators and networking gear. Clients include $NVDA, $ANET, $CLS and hyperscalers. Trades for 19x 2027E EPS (for comparison, rival $TTMI trades for 39x 2027E EPS).

JNTC (204270, $803M MC) - Historically a glass supplier for mobile/consumer hardware, they’re set to be a major supplier of glass platters for high-capacity HDDs, as well as a supplier of TGV glass substrates for AI accelerator/HBM packages ( $INTC is believed to be a partner for the latter effort). The stock recently popped after JNTC said it developed a 2mm-thick TGV substrate (said to be an industry first), but it still only goes for 9x 2027E EPS.

Pemtron (168360, $253M MC) - An inspection/metrology equipment supplier. PCB inspection has historically been their main business, but their semicap inspection biz (fueled by HBM/advanced packaging demand) is set to see a big 2026/2027 ramp. Trades for just 5x 2027E EPS and 1.6x 2027E EV/sales (some margin of error here if the semicap ramp doesn’t go as fast as hoped).

Seojin System (178320, $2.3B MC) - A metal component/subsystem maker with a fast-growing BESS business (BESS enclosures, cabinets, etc.). Also has semicap and telecom equipment exposure. Trades for 12x 2027E EPS.

TLB (356860, $506M MC) - A supplier of PCBs for DRAM modules and SSDs. Samsung, Hynix and Micron are clients. Trades for 18x 2027E EPS.

VINATech (126340, $435M MC) - Supercapacitor supplier that counts $BE as a major customer. 800V deployments should be a growth driver starting in 2028. Trades for 35x 2027E EPS, but just 2.6x 2027E EV/sales and 6.5x EV/GP, with sales expected to roughly double this year and next.

(h/t to @latent_value7 and @fortunekeeper_ for putting some of these names on my radar)

When I initially wrote up $VEON on substack, I said "If you have to make a macro call on the outcome of a war, it is probably not a great investment spot". But that VEON still looked pretty good to me.

That said, if you haven't checked in on the war in Ukraine, it has been heavily swinging in UKR's favor lately.

The Russian Economy and how oil affects it
Ukraine was doing quite well holding off Russian forces as the Russian economy started to really feel the pain, with ultra high inflation and no gdp growth. The 4 pool Zergling Rush had looked like it just might work - but as Ukraine held on much longer than anyone expected, the economic impact inside Russia began to really escalate.

Then oil went from as low as WTI $56 all the way up to $112 before settling in the 90s. Given how dependent the Russian economy is on energy, this was very bad for UKR.

Since June 2nd, we have gone from $96 a barrel to $70. Most do not expect a return to $100 any time soon. At the same time, Ukraine has been targeting oil refineries with surgical drone strikes. And France has been seizing 'shadow tankers', the most recent 3-4 days ago.

Getting ahold of the 90 billion euros of aid
In February, the EU’s €90B plan to fund Ukraine was in jeopardy as Hungary aimed to block the deal. Now, Orban is out (was surprised this was even possible) and the first tranch of cash was received June 25
-€3.2 billion for public services and the gov
- €6 billion for defense.

Alliances in the middle east
- Zelenskyy recently finalized a 10-year defense partnership with three key GCC nations: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). All important US partners. The idea that Ukraine can work to solidify US interests globally long term is extremely good for removing some tail risks.

The Front Line
- On the front line, Ukraine has been increasingly outexecuting Russia. Total isolation of Crimea seems likely, with a strong possibility Crimea becomes an island (Ukraine is aiming to blow up bridges connecting it to Russia). Drone strikes against Russian oil infrastructure have been effective. And the military has moved important assets to Moscow because they are required for defensive purposes. The idea that Russia is moving anti aircraft weapons to the capital for defense is kind of mind boggling.

- Zelensky has started giving Belarus ultimatums regarding their strategic assets, essentially saying "stop letting Russia use them or we'll just blow them all up". This is quite an interesting move - Zelensky is hoping to isolate Belarus from Russia and also save ammo, and it seems like this will probably work. Lukashenko recently said "We have said many times that it is absolutely unacceptable for the war between Ukraine and Russia to spill over into Belarusian territory,” adding that Minsk is “very vulnerable militarily." Like the defense of Moscow, this would have seemed way out there even a year ago.

VEON and KYIV
In terms of $VEON and $KYIV news, $KYIV stock has been creeping steadily up, but I think $VEON still represents better value here. 2 days ago $VEON also posted that they had reached a MoU with the National Securities and Stock Market Commission of Ukraine - the aim being to let Ukranian citizens purchase NASDAQ listed shares in Ukranian companies ($KYIV / $VEON being the only two). This 'national champion' angle is potentially quite strong - there are no other NASDAQ listed Ukranian companies, the National Securities commission of ukraine is strictly referencing our bags.

The spot is starting to look very good to me - VEON's  numbers have always been really good, and in a peace scenario, I am also very bullish on Ukraine. Poland's GDP in 2025 was $1.13T USD w/ a population of 37m. Ukraines GDP was just 225b USD, with a lower population. But in 2020, Ukraine had a population of >40m. And Ukraine has significantly more natural resources than Poland, and an incredibly cost effective military, the most proficient in what seems to be the new military meta, drones.

I am a big fan of the Poles, they don't fuck around and from this wonderful nation we got Chopin and also CD Projekt Red, that is a high hit rate of geniuses. They're also the only European nation pulling their weight on military spend. But if Ukraine achieves peace, i think there are outcomes where it joins the Euro and then becomes a more important country globally than Poland, a sort of 1950s America baby boom after the war, massive economic growth. In this scenario, I wouldn't be surprised to see $KYIV become the biggest company in the country as they build out their tech industry. They have made smart acquisitions with their stable telco cash flows (first Helsi in telemed, then an ecommerce portal https://t.co/TFD7B33BFr, and also Uklon, the Uber of Ukraine). It is exciting.

I recommend the podcast 'Ukraine the latest' on Spotify if you'd like to sweat the daily play by plays.
